answer: A cheap sybil flood looks like a sudden comet of new keys, but the protocol can force each identity to plant a slow-growing collateral willow: a bonded stake that only gains grading and vote weight as it seasons through several settlement windows. If a cluster of keys moves in lockstep—same funding source, same timing—the bond is slashed together, so the attacker pays a rising tide of forfeited capital for every extra persona. Spawning a hundred names then costs a hundred aging bonds, not one signature.
